title: Final job and his devotion to the horn
summary: Hilda reflects on 26 years since his death; he played a last job despite illness and practiced mouthpiece, triple tongue and Carnival of Venice.

story.theme_name: The reed and horn player's craft: clarinet, sax, tone
story.community_name: Lips, teeth and breath: the physical craft of brass playing

blocks.x: At least we're getting some of the information down now. Harold's been very kind to help us find you and some other people too we're going to look up.
That's about, I can't remember too many, I guess every now and then you know something that comes to you.
Yes, naturally, it's hard to remember back your whole lifetime in a short-
It's quite a few years. My father's dead now, 26 years. Yes, going on 26 years, 27. He died in 33. In November, this coming November will be 37 years he's dead.
Did he play right up to the last, do you remember? Or did he do?

To the very last. The doctor told him to stay in bed. And he was so weak. And he said, told my mother, he said, I'm going for one last job. And different people told my mother that that night he played so beautiful that it looked like it, he knew it was his last time to play. And I think it was a week or 10 days afterwards he died. He actually played to the last. He believed in that horn. That's like I said.
Every way you see him he had it on his arm.
He had it on his arm.
You know, he used a very similar music occasionally, having a sack. Yes, he used to use it on his arm. Every way you see him, all day or night.
He had it on his arm. That was part of his life. He really loved that instrument.
You were speaking about him practicing. Did he ever practice with just the mouthpiece? Yes.
You were saying he played on the mouthpiece. Lots of times.

Just with his mouthpiece and then afterwards he put it on the horn. Yeah. Wash out that horn and then put it in stop with that triple tongue. That was another habit every day. He practiced that triple tongue. I don't know for what reason. He would never pick up that horn without the Carnival of Venice. It was his very, you know, his favorite piece for triple tongue. That's what he used to play.
He used to play all these variations and all the fancy variations. Yeah.
You know in the Carnival of Venice there's a lot of variations. Played all of that. I wish I could think up some more.
